# Verification analysis: guest-network-isolation-rhel7

Job: `2026-09-05__08-02-31`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `lan-a` carries trusted hosts and `lan-b` is for guests; `node2` is on the
> first and `node3` on the second, with `node1` between them. Guests must be
> able to reach services `node1` itself offers them, such as DNS, but no host
> on `lan-b` may open a connection to any host on `lan-a`. Trusted hosts keep
> full access in the other direction.

- Systems: **1 openwrt + 2 rhel7.9**
- Networks: **mgmt, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node2**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `guest-network-isolation-rhel7__aBapTVM`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor implemented node1 as a router between lan-a (node2, trusted) and lan-b (node3, guest) using OpenWrt UCI firewall zones (lan_a forward=ACCEPT, lan_b forward=REJECT) plus a single lan_a->lan_b forwarding rule, and enabled dnsmasq on both new interfaces. All four material outcomes from the task -- trusted-to-guest full access, guest-to-trusted blocking, guest DNS reachability to node1, and trusted DNS reachability to node1 -- are directly demonstrated with live functional tests (curl success/refusal, DNS queries) corroborated by nftables ruleset inspection. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for all three nodes with observed boot-identity changes and recovered state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots; node2/node3 recovery included a live DNS re-test, while node1's recovery check was config-only rather than a repeated functional isolation test. Hygiene is good overall; the only notable blemish is two bounded, fully-reverted firewalld troubleshooting mutations on node2/node3 en route to the final fix.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.800 | 0.850 | 54/6 (+3 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Trusted hosts on lan-a (node2) keep full access to guest hosts on lan-b (node3)
  - **Why:** node1 nftables forward_lan_a jumps to accept_to_lan_b (cmd-a93c97870b6f41d3). After the executor corrected node2's own host firewall (which was independently blocking inbound test traffic, unrelated to the router policy), a curl from node2 to node3:8000 succeeded with a full directory listing (cmd-f5f133149ec74305), directly demonstrating trusted-to-guest connectivity at both the router and end-to-end level.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a93c97870b6f41d3`, `cmd-a451dca3512d4814`, `cmd-7342196bea1545e7`, `cmd-f5f133149ec74305`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** No host on lan-b (node3, guest) may open a connection to any host on lan-a (node2, trusted)
  - **Why:** curl from node3 to node2:8000 was actively refused with a TCP RST (cmd-3ba1f4511cbd478f), and node1's nftables ruleset was inspected to confirm the lan_b forward chain unconditionally jumps to reject/handle_reject with no lan_b->lan_a forwarding rule present (cmd-2ab18e02ecae4a03).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3ba1f4511cbd478f`, `cmd-2ab18e02ecae4a03`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Guests (lan-b/node3) must be able to reach services node1 itself offers, e.g. DNS
  - **Why:** dnsmasq confirmed listening on the lan-b address 10.10.2.1:53 (cmd-0cb2c28aad4f4330), and a raw DNS query issued from node3 to 10.10.2.1:53 received a valid response (cmd-88a5c491583a4c9b).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0cb2c28aad4f4330`, `cmd-88a5c491583a4c9b`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Trusted hosts (lan-a/node2) can also reach node1's own services (e.g. DNS)
  - **Why:** A DNS query from node2 to node1's lan-a address 10.10.1.1:53 returned a valid response (cmd-afec77ee05b44b2c), and was re-verified again after node2's reboot (cmd-0f75d709f19242d5).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-afec77ee05b44b2c`, `cmd-0f75d709f19242d5`
- **req-5 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes (node1, node2, node3) with pre-restart baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered state
  - **Why:** All three nodes show a captured pre-restart boot_id/config baseline, an explicit reboot invocation, a directly observed different post-restart boot_id, and recovered interface/firewall/DNS state. node2 and node3 additionally had DNS functionality re-tested end-to-end post-reboot. node1's post-restart check confirmed configuration (interfaces, firewall zones, forwarding rule, dnsmasq, and the reject_to_lan_b nftables chain) but did not repeat the live curl-based guest-block/trusted-allow functional test after its own reboot, so its recovery evidence is config-level rather than fully behavioral. This is cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots, which show matching boot_id transitions for all three nodes.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7d4542de290042c6`, `cmd-982d02354b574318`, `cmd-32aa19f223264438`, `cmd-49ec4f9cc2de4a0d`, `cmd-75d4af033ba44121`, `cmd-b377d849c3ca4f93`, `cmd-9032113879144729`, `cmd-0f75d709f19242d5`, `cmd-abd02c7d13f54eec`, `cmd-bad9c9065ffb4c75`, `cmd-9729ea46e3a5471e`, `cmd-79f8ccfa64c5483c`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node3:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Most state-changing commands map directly to the task (node1 UCI network/firewall/dhcp configuration, node2/node3 nmcli interface configuration, restart-protocol reboots) or to bounded, fully-reverted test setup (temporary HTTP servers on node2/node3, killed via cmd-8c924a31757a4e97 and cmd-db79460c68ed4a27). Two mutations stand out as unnecessary troubleshooting experiments: cmd-a451dca3512d4814 added the guest network 10.10.2.0/24 as a trusted source in node2's public firewalld zone, and cmd-68f88cf9c64f42d4 did the symmetric thing on node3 with the trusted network 10.10.1.0/24 -- both intended to unblock a 'No route to host' error that was actually a routing/zone issue. Both were reverted moments later (cmd-7342196bea1545e7, cmd-632bd2a022df460a) in favor of moving eth1 into the 'trusted' NetworkManager/firewalld zone, which is a more defensible fix since the requirement's isolation boundary is enforced at node1, not at the RHEL hosts. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary package/service state changes were found in the lifecycle diff (only expected reboot.log and systemd-private temp dirs, plus dnsmasq/dropbear/uhttpd socket churn from the restart).

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-a451dca3512d4814`, `cmd-68f88cf9c64f42d4`, `cmd-7342196bea1545e7`, `cmd-632bd2a022df460a`, `cmd-8c924a31757a4e97`, `cmd-db79460c68ed4a27`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- node1's post-restart verification checked configuration state (interfaces, firewall zones, forwarding rule, dnsmasq, nftables reject chain) but did not repeat the live curl-based guest-blocked/trusted-allowed functional test after its own reboot, so full behavioral recovery on node1 specifically is inferred from configuration rather than directly re-observed.
- The executor made two temporary firewalld zone/source mutations on node2 and node3 while debugging an unrelated 'No route to host' issue; both were reverted, but per evaluation guidance they are still counted as unnecessary mutations in the hygiene assessment even though no residue remained.
- Package-health checks for node2 and node3 timed out at every lifecycle capture point (before_prepare and after_executor), so package/dependency state cannot be independently confirmed as unchanged, though no other evidence suggests package-level modification.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.800); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
